## Contact-timed Hebbian updating (contact-gate-v1)

E133 uses the three original saved controllers with zero training. Each family replays both initial rules with identical observations, imposed actions and received feedback across native updating, a locally observed contact gate, equally sparse randomly timed updates and a reopened-delay ablation. After sixteen common contacts and eight stationary or reversed contacts, local choice and fresh fifty-turn solo behavior are measured immediately and after 33 empty turns. All solo readouts use ordinary learning, so this measures transfer of the carried state, not live use of the gate.

Every assigned life counts. Two rule replays are averaged within each of 64 independent families before sample standard errors and paired contrasts. A dead exposure state gets no fresh body: local and signed solo choice are zero, with no contact retained. Solo Y is first food minus first poison. The sparse schedule draws one offset independently in each four-turn block and can coincide with contact feedback by chance; its overlap is descriptive.

Retention requires verified immediate acquisition plus the registered delayed comparison. Every acquisition, retention, transfer, stationary and survival criterion must pass in each of the three lineages. Stationary-adjusted solo differences are descriptive.

Replicated contact gate: **FAIL** (0/3 lineages).

A full pass would justify a separately registered autonomous deployment check before bounded equal-budget selection of a heritable between-contact learning gain. Failed immediate acquisition points to feedback use. A local retention effect without transfer does not advance this design into evolutionary training. Failure to distinguish equal sparsity or the reopened delay retires this setting without tuning on these assignments.

One ± is one family SE, paired for comparisons. All rates use fractions. Immediate and delayed solo probes are separate clones; neither changes the source state.

## Voluntary access to both alternatives (voluntary-offers-v1)

E132 uses the three original saved controllers with one creature per life. Every family replays both initial rules. After eight common nearby eight-turn offers, copies receive eight further offers crossing nearby versus random-distance placement with stationary versus reversed rules. The creature chooses every action. Local choice and a fresh fifty-turn solo probe measure what transfers beyond the presentation apparatus.

Every initially assigned birth counts. Two rule replays are averaged inside each of 64 independent families before means, paired differences and sample standard errors. Both-color exposure counts actual contacts during the continuation, including a contact that causes death. The survival safeguard is measured at exposure tick 128; survival after the empty feedback tick 129 is shown separately. Dead readout states score zero for local and signed solo choice, with no-contact retained in the assigned denominator. Solo Y is first food minus first poison.

All three lineages must pass the registered preference, access, solo-transfer and survival criteria. There is no policy-time ratio and no new training.

Replicated voluntary access: **FAIL** (0/3 lineages).

A pass would support a contribution from easier access to the alternatives in this apparatus. It would leave calorie intake, visual stimulation and feedback contributions unresolved. When access improves but transfer fails, the result points to examining feedback use; a failed access manipulation cannot establish a memory defect.

All rates use fractions; one ± is one family SE. Initial-rule views are descriptive. Intake counts each consumed color per assigned life, and realized energy is the sum of signed actual energy changes during the 64 continuation turns, including clipped gains.

## Feedback-timed exploration (timed-exploration-v1)

E131 compares the same saved generation-200 controller with unchanged actions, drought-timed exploration, and outcome-independent exploration with the same nominal quota. Independent random phase delays avoid alignment with the hidden switch at turn 150. All four original animals and both initial rules count inside each of 64 independent families per lineage.

First-food latency uses offsets 0–49 in [150,200), or 50 without food, including death. Each fifty-turn Q is the first item: food +1, poison -1, no contact zero. Every lineage must improve latency and direct late reversal Q over both controls above two paired SE, retain positive adaptive late Q, and improve history-adjusted late Q by at least 0.05 and above two paired SE. Stationary late Q and survival in both histories must retain lower paired two-SE bounds above -0.05. The development runtime ceiling is a separate adoption condition.

## Founder and descendant autonomous reversal (founder-reversal-v1)

E130 pairs each original E103 founder with its generation-200 descendant in stationary and unannounced reversal worlds. Four original animals choose every action for 300 turns, with the food rule changing before consumption at turn 150. Each family replays both initial rules with the same world and development randomness across both genotypes and histories.

Q scores each animal's first item in each fifty-turn window as +1 for food, -1 for poison and zero for no item, including death before contact. Average all four animals and both initial rules inside each of 64 independent families before computing a mean or sample SE. Pre, early and late windows are [100,150), [150,200) and [250,300). Endpoints and lineages are never pooled into extra samples.

Every lineage must have positive descendant pre-switch and late reversal Q above two SE. The descendant's reversal improvement from early to late, its late advantage over the founder, and the genotype-by-history recovery interaction K must each be at least 0.05 and strictly above two paired SE. Each descendant-minus-founder lower two-SE bound must exceed -0.05 for pre Q, stationary late Q and final survival in both histories. All three lineages must pass every criterion.

## Hebbian updates during the empty interval (retention-intervention-v1)

E129 compares normal and temporarily Hebbian-off retention in the original plastic controllers, with paired reversed and stationary histories on fresh families. The immediate snapshot is shared. Only Hebbian changes during the 33 empty turns are disabled in the intervention; prediction updates continue and Hebbian updates resume in the fifty-turn free grid. The fixed-weight controls have only their normal trajectory and remain descriptive.

The primary effect requires a Hebbian-off minus normal signed-preference gain of at least 0.025 and strictly more than two paired SE in all three lineages. Local rescue additionally requires every original E128 local criterion in the intervention. Transfer rescue additionally requires the E128 grid criterion and a positive first-food gain above two paired SE in those same three lineages. The original 0.05 retention-loss margin is unchanged. All uncertainties average both initial rules and local placements inside independent families before paired statistics.

## Retention after guided evidence (retention-diagnostic-v1)

E128 compares the same original E103 plastic and E113 fixed-weight controllers on new families. After sixteen changed or stationary encounters, the complete living state continues for 0, 1 or 33 active turns on an empty torus. Ordinary body feedback, recurrence and lifetime updates continue; no items appear. Discarded local probes and a fresh-body, fifty-turn grid readout use paired layouts and randomness across histories and delays. There is no new training or brain mechanism.

All errors are one sample SE across independent families, after averaging twelve local placements and both initial rules inside each family. S is the reversal-history signed food preference; C is its paired reversal-minus-stationary contrast. G is first-food success across all assigned lives; Y is first-food minus first-poison success, with no contact or prior death scoring zero.

Local retention requires S and C at both 0 and 33 turns to be at least 0.10 and strictly above two SE. Grid retention requires positive Y above two SE at both times and a 33-turn paired G advantage of at least 0.10 and above two SE. Each reversal-history change from 0 to 33 must also have a lower two-SE bound strictly above -0.05. All three lineages must pass local retention; the same three must pass local and grid criteria for the combined milestone. The one-turn snapshot and old-food preference before reversal are descriptive. Fixed-weight controls are secondary.

## Guided evidence and fresh-grid transfer (encounter-diagnostic-v1)

E127 uses the original three E103 plastic controllers and matched E113 recurrent controllers. There is no training or fitted readout. Each independent family replays both initial rules on the same counterbalanced guided-contact script. The boundary follows eight or sixteen contacts; sixteen further contacts provide stationary or reversed feedback. Choice probes use discarded clones at zero, two, eight and sixteen post-boundary contacts. The grid readout preserves the unprobed brain in a fresh body and ordinary grid for fifty turns.

All uncertainties use independent families after averaging both rule replays and, for local probes, twelve ordered color placements. S is target-food action probability minus other-color action probability. G is all-assigned first-food success in fifty turns. Y is +1 for first food, -1 for first poison and zero for no contact or death before contact; its SE retains covariance within each family. Net return is a separate whole-grid endpoint. A weak grid readout can reflect context, fresh body, search or memory effects and cannot isolate navigation alone.

Development, incomplete panels and panels awaiting independent verification have no replicated scientific decision. Local reversal, transfer in the same lineages, and Hebbian contribution are separate decisions. A failed threshold means this assay did not establish that effect.

The registered comparison uses E127-A0-recovery1, E127-A1 and E127-A2. The failed original A0 prefix remains preserved and is excluded from inference; its eleven families are not added to the recovery's 128-family denominator. The corrected four-family rehearsal is for verification and timing only.

## Matched from-blank reversal evolution (reversal-evolution-v1)

E126 targets 200 attempted rounds in each of three plastic and three direct recurrent lineages. Both use population 128 and four base worlds replayed under both initial rules: eight actual lives per candidate. The objective is mean individual minimum late return across those rule replays. Genomes start from their original blank initializers. There is no social readout or new mechanism. Equal scores receive average ranks; all-tied attempts consume worlds and advance RNG without changing the genome, Adam moments or informative-update counter. Immutable segments preserve both counters. Development benchmarks measure throughput only.

No held-out world opens before all six targets reach attempt 200. Final panels use 128 independent base worlds per seed pair, each under both rules and stationary/reversal interventions. Errors use base-world units. The formal architecture comparison uses combined standard errors; the paired difference is reported separately. At least two same seeds must pass the architecture, positive late return, late first-food and postflip Hebbian-lesion criteria. All three plastic seeds must pass the joint-survival floor and relative lower-two-SE screen. Partial panels and short training segments cannot decide the rung or authorize an added mechanism.

Complete three-seed rung decision: **undecided**.

## Three public-behavior handoffs (social-transmission-v1)

E124 freezes each original E103 genotype and its E123 training-calibrated scalar. A solitary founder supplies its last 150 public frames to a newborn. Three successive cohorts watch, act alone, and supply their last 150 public frames to the next newborn. Only the predecessor arm teaches the next cohort. All assigned chains remain, including dead teachers and empty late footage. Fresh bodies, brains and solo layouts are drawn for each cohort. No weights, internal beliefs, rewards or hidden labels cross the handoff.

First-food accuracy scores one for food and zero for first poison or no meal. Each mean and standard error uses independent chains; paired comparisons keep entire chains intact. Intervals show mean minus/plus two paired standard errors. Retained efficacy requires first-food gains over yoked and belief-reset movies strictly above two SE in every cohort. The survival lower two-SE bound must strictly exceed -0.10 against every same-cohort control, and for cohort 3 versus cohort 1. This ten-percentage-point tolerance is a confidence screen; it does not prove equal survival.

Cumulative improvement additionally requires cohort 3 to beat both cohort 1 and the cohort 3 repeated-founder control by more than two paired SE. All gates must hold in all three lineages. Retention alone supports persistence through these three handoffs. Both gates support net improvement over these three cohorts, not perpetual or monotonic improvement. The genotype and engineered readout remain fixed. Development and incomplete attempts have no scientific decision.

## Calibrated engineered social readout (social-belief-readout-v1)

E123 retains the original E103 genomes and adds an engineered scalar belief with a fixed local action readout. There are zero ES generations and no genome mutation. One scalar lambda is selected from nine fixed values using public movie contacts and an unassisted pupil's own first outcome on calibration worlds. The complete calibration evidence and selection are frozen before opening disjoint evaluation worlds. Calibration losses and coverage below are fitting diagnostics, not held-out performance.

Each held-out family has six paired arms. First food is one for food and zero for poison or no meal, across all assigned families. No-meal first-choice latency is capped at step 301. Means and ± SEM use families as the independent unit; contrasts use paired family differences. The observed arm must beat every one of the five controls by strictly more than two paired SEM on first food, with survival differences at least minus two paired SEM. All three lineages must pass the complete intersection gate. A parent-only benefit cannot override a failed control or survival comparison. Development and incomplete attempts have no scientific verdict.

The belief-reset control changes only the added belief; birth-parent uses the original unassisted birth state. A pass supports useful public information through this calibrated engineered readout; it does not show the unchanged hidden network invented social learning. A failed gate ends this version without retuning on its evaluation worlds.

## Saved-controller transfer to randomized rule reversal (reversal-random-v1)

E125 changes only the hidden food interpretation at time 100, 125, 150 or 175, with 16 families per initial-rule/time cell in each final lineage. Every arm has paired stationary and reversal copies; the stationary copy uses the same shadow boundary for analysis. No new genome optimization or scalar calibration occurs. The fixed primary is the E123 prepared observer, with its original genome and pinned calibration. Its belief is not reset at the hidden flip.

Windows relative to the boundary are pre [-50,0), early [0,50), and late [50,100). First contact is food scores one; poison, death or no contact scores zero across all assigned families. Means and ± SEM use independent families; all contrasts use paired family differences. Contact-conditioned accuracy includes its explicit encounter denominator and is undefined when no items were eaten.

The primary passes only if late reversal success is at least 0.60 and exceeds 0.50 by more than two SEM; recovery (late minus early in reversal, minus the same change in stationary) exceeds two paired SEM; and the lower two-SEM bounds for late-success and end-survival reversal-minus-stationary differences both exceed -0.10. Every criterion must pass in all three lineages. These bounds are a transfer screen, not proof of equivalence. A good immediate response without the registered recovery contrast still fails this gate. Development and incomplete attempts have no scientific verdict.

This measures saved-controller transfer, Phase 3(a). The formal rung remains undecided: it still requires registered evolution from blank across three seeds, a matched fair baseline comparison, and a mechanism lesion. The neutral selected birth state is exactly birth_parent and is reused, not another replicate. Only the birth_parent versus direct_baseline panel has matched birth information. Prepared-versus-direct scores have unequal prior information and cannot establish architecture superiority.

## Information in public demonstrations (social-channel-v1)

E121 uses fixed readers of 150 public frames after a teacher's 150 practice turns. The track reader uses consecutive visible teacher positions; the scene reader uses item-image motion only. Both predict the most frequently contacted visible item color as food. Ties and no votes earn expected accuracy of one half. Every family is retained. Means use independent families; all ± values are standard errors of the mean (SEM), and control contrasts use paired within-family differences. Fractions are proportions, while votes and identifiable steps are mean counts per family. The tie fraction includes movies with no votes.

The channel gate uses only the track reader's observed arm: coverage at least 0.50, expected accuracy at least 0.60, accuracy minus chance (0.50) strictly greater than two family SEM, and observed-minus-yoked accuracy strictly greater than two paired SEM. All four criteria must pass separately in all three lineages. A pass shows this fixed reader can use the public stimulus; it does not show an agent learned socially. A failure does not establish that every possible reader would fail. The scene reader and other control comparisons are diagnostics. Development and incomplete attempts have no scientific verdict.

## Observer evolution with fixed teachers (social-observer-train-v1)

E122 branch O attempts ten observer ES rounds from each original genome while its demonstrator stays fixed. Equal scores receive average ranks. All-tied rounds consume their worlds and advance the random stream while preserving genome, moments and optimizer-update count. The table reports informative updates separately from attempted rounds. Held-out gains are observed minus each comparator, in first-food probability with paired family standard errors. A lineage passes only if all four gains exceed two SE and every survival difference is at least minus two SE. All assigned families contribute, including no-meal outcomes. All three lineages must pass. Development and incomplete records have no scientific verdict.

## Observational learning and solo transfer (social-learning-v1)

E120 tests one newborn per independent world family after 150 observation frames from an experienced teacher. Its solo test lasts 300 turns in a fresh world. The primary measure is first solo meal being food per assigned newborn; poison and no meal both count as zero. The observed movie is compared with yoked item colors, a time-matched blank movie and a scene-only movie. Each lineage must exceed every control by more than two paired family standard errors, with each all-assigned survival difference at least minus two SE. The table shows proportions and observed-minus-control differences. All three lineages must pass; development and incomplete attempts have no scientific verdict.

## Evolution with inherited experience (inherited-evolution-v1)

E119 continues each E118 optimizer for ten updates. Before each update, the current mean genome adds its training donors' acquired sensory-to-output changes to a bounded archive. All candidates then receive that archive. The final child with its latest archive is compared with its immediate parent and previous archive on 128 fresh paired worlds. Death and nonarrival count as 301 turns; inside births are excluded from latency and retained in survival. A seed passes when saved turns exceed two paired family-cluster standard errors and survival changes by at least minus two SE. All three seeds must pass. Additional controls hold the genome or archive fixed and remain in each summary. Development and incomplete attempts have no scientific decision.

## Shelter evolution (shelter-evolution-v1)

E118 evolves each original A genome for ten generations and compares its final descendant with its parent on 128 paired unseen worlds. Both use the same shelter ecology and persistence trait. Births outside shelter contribute to the capped first living arrival time. Death and nonarrival count as 301 turns. The reported reduction is parent minus descendant, with a family-cluster standard error. The survival difference is descendant minus parent among all assigned creatures. Each seed passes if latency improves by more than two paired standard errors and survival falls by at most two paired standard errors. All three seeds must pass. The development benchmark and incomplete runs have no scientific decision. Genome changes describe mutation and selection; the paired test measures their outcome.

## Cold donor inheritance (cold-donor-v1)

E117 uses fixed original A genomes in the same full ecology for both splits. Each independent family has one cold donor life and paired newborn recipient arms, with persistence off. Restricted first-shelter-arrival latency excludes agents born inside shelter; nonarrival, including death before a living arrival, counts as 301 steps. Latency reduction is fresh minus inherited, and survival difference is inherited minus fresh. Estimates are means ± paired family SE; pooled outside-born latency uses a family-cluster ratio SE. Each seed requires latency improvement strictly above two SE and survival difference at least minus two SE. All three final seed decisions must pass for the study gate. The four-family development benchmark has no gate; incomplete attempts have no pooled estimates or decision. Other registered metrics and compressed family evidence remain in each run folder.

## Paired objective continuation (paired-train-v1)

## EVAL v6 paired learning-rate comparison

Original starts, six fixed E116 final genomes and five references share fresh v6 worlds. Values are independent base-world means ± SE, never pooled across training seeds. The gate requires candidate individual-minimum return to exceed both control and unchanged start by strictly more than two paired SE in every seed, with candidate-minus-start joint survival at least minus two paired SE. Equality fails return checks and is allowed at the survival boundary; this does not prove equivalent survival. Incomplete or invalid attempts remain undecided. All 30 registered contrasts and per-rule survival/encounter data remain in the aggregate summary and raw files. Reversal outcomes cannot substitute for the gate, and E115's failed gate is unchanged.

Survival values are fractions. Development rows use tiny seed-41 fixtures only. These descriptive measurements do not replace the failed E113 gate. Per-rule accuracy, deaths, encounters, all 15 planned A-minus-direct contrasts and raw events remain in the run folder. Incomplete attempts retain their completed conditions and show undefined paired estimates.

## EVAL v3 diagnostics

Saved genomes only; 256 fresh worlds per panel. SE treats each world-family as one cluster. Greedy fractions use a paired world-level delta-method SE. Greedy knows the current rule but sees only the local patch; it is not an optimal-policy bound. Repeated policy rows use the same worlds and are not independent replications. Meal counts, survivor-conditioned bins and raw events are preserved in each run's summary.json and events.npz.

## Direct recurrent baseline (direct-v1)

The direct-rnn-v1 genome encodes fixed recurrent weights; hidden states still change during life. No lifetime synaptic, predictor or structural updates occur. Final rows use the same 256 EVAL v3 worlds and references; development rows use tiny fixtures and seed 41, never held-out worlds. Each uncertainty is a world-family SE for that fixed genome, not variability across training seeds. Raw events, full diagnostics and initial/final weight magnitudes remain in each run folder.
